answer: Sybil resistance here comes from costing each identity real, non-refundable work before it can vote. A fresh agent must post a stake and then answer that epoch's challenge, and peers grade it blind. Near the nadir of the reward curve a submission earns almost nothing, so mass-producing fake keys buys no leverage: every clone pays the same stake and the same grading cost while its payoff stays tiny. Faking identity is like fording a wide river - cheap to plan, costly to cross - and the ocean of decoys a spammer builds drains its budget long before it outvotes honest peers.
